segments.title: Opening: date, names and recording setup
segments.summary: Alcorn gives his full name and the date, 30 November 1960, at the library seminar room; the interviewers introduce themselves.

segments.title: Don Albert band records: personnel, growl trumpet and arrangers
segments.summary: Playing the Don Albert records, Alcorn recalls that all the sides were made in one session, who played in the band, the growl trumpeter, and Geechee Robinson's arrangement; Billy Douglas is praised as a trumpeter.

segments.title: Jimmy Johnson's bass style
segments.summary: Alcorn describes the bassist on the record as a fine player who picked and bowed, especially on waltzes and slow tunes, never slapping.

segments.title: Paul Barnes, his mutes, and pianist Lloyd Glenn
segments.summary: Alcorn talks about trumpeter Paul Barnes, his mutes, and how Barnes left a job and Alcorn stayed on in his place. Alcorn also identifies pianist Lloyd Glenn and recalls recording with him in California.

segments.title: Cut mute, high F endings and playing first trumpet
segments.summary: Discussion of the cut mute, how arrangers wrote high F endings for the trumpets, and who hit the high F on the Shine record.

segments.title: Recording with one microphone
segments.summary: Alcorn reflects on how the band recorded with a single mic and would like to hear it re-recorded.

segments.title: Arrangers, then birth, family, teacher McCollum and brass band funerals
segments.summary: One long block: the band's arrangers and soloists, then Alcorn's 1912 birth in New Orleans, his musical family, teacher George McCollum, and old brass band funerals and clarinetists. It cannot be divided.

segments.title: First brass band job with the Excelsior and marching technique
segments.summary: Alcorn recalls his first brass band job, sent to sub with the Excelsior Brass Band around 1929-30, the lineup that day, the band's instrumentation, and how bass drum and left-foot marching work for 6/8 and 2/4 marches.

segments.chapter: Brass bands and first dance band
segments.title: Drilling groups, no military service, first dance band
segments.summary: Alcorn explains the parade drilling groups such as the Odd Fellows, says he was not in the service, and names his first dance band, the Sunny Style Syncopators; the tape runs out.
